samples.summary: New docs `readOnly` presence gate has no test at all
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore` gained a `readOnly` constructor flag and two new early-returns (`publishResolvedLocalCursor` ~L1263 and `updateCursorPos` ~L3196) that suppress the presence `doc.update()` for a share-link viewer; `docs-view.tsx` now passes `Boolean(readOnly)`. The existing suite `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` contains no occurrence of `readOnly` (grep returned no matches), and no other frontend test constructs the store with the second argument. The sibling sheets gate got a whole new file (`yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts`); the docs one got none, so a regression that reintroduces the viewer presence write — which per the diff's own reasoning wedges the viewer's entire sync — ships silently.

The new guard `if (this._readOnly) { this.worksheet.render(); return; }` changes behavior (repaint but no recalc/persist) and is the engine-side backstop for `sheet-view.tsx`'s `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)`. `packages/sheets/test/sheet/cross-sheet-calculation.test.ts` and `cross-sheet-cycle.test.ts` only call `sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas()` on the model (lines 138/176/212/228/258), never the `Spreadsheet` view method, and no test in the sheets package constructs a read-only `Spreadsheet` to assert the pass is skipped. Neither is the call-site change in `sheet-view.tsx` (`runRemoteSync(!readOnly)`, `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : …)`) covered by any frontend test — grep for `readOnly` in packages/frontend/tests returns no sheet-view file.

samples.summary: Component-level read-only presence gates (pdf activePage, board selection, slides broadcast, mobile-slides seed) have no tests
samples.evidence: Four new gates are added with no coverage: `onActivePageChange` (`if (readOnly || …) return`, pdf-collab.tsx:133), `board-view.tsx`'s `onSelectionChange` `if (readOnly) return`, `slides-view.tsx`'s `broadcast` `if (readOnlyMount) return`, and `mobile-slides-view.tsx` passing `readOnly: mode === 'view'` into `ensureSlidesRoot`. `packages/frontend/tests/app/files/pdf-collab.test.tsx` never mentions `activePage` (grep found it only in src), and grep for `readOnly` across packages/frontend/tests yields only shared-header-status, the two pdf provider tests, the slides store test and docs read-only UI tests — none of these components' presence paths. Only the unit-level helpers (`ensureSlidesRoot`, `initialRoot`) are tested, so the flag plumbing into them is unverified.

samples.summary: `CommentPopover`'s new `readOnly` prop and new message branch are untested
samples.evidence: `isReadOnly = readOnly || currentUser === null` and the new copy ("You have view-only access to this document.") are the UI half of the viewer-comment fix, but grep for `CommentPopover` across packages/frontend finds only source files (sheet-view.tsx, yorkie-store.ts, the component itself, docs-view.tsx, DocsCommentPopover.tsx) — no test file renders it. So the claim in sheet-view.tsx's comment (signed-in non-member no longer gets compose/reply/resolve affordances) rests only on the store-level `assertWritable` throws, which are tested; the UI hiding is not.

samples.summary: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` and the scripts' `sideTokenInjector` have no tests, including the missing-secret path
samples.evidence: There is no `yorkie-service-token.spec.ts` (glob of packages/backend/src/yorkie/*.ts lists the module but no spec). `signYorkieServiceToken` and `yorkieServiceTokenInjector` are exercised indirectly via auth.service.spec.ts and yorkie.service.spec.ts, but `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` (its `JWT_SECRET`-unset → warn + `undefined` branch, and the unvalidated `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN as ms.StringValue` cast) and `sideTokenInjector` in `scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts` (the no-cross-fallback rule the doc-comment makes the centerpiece of this change) are covered by nothing. Also unverified: that the two sides' injectors sign with different secrets rather than sharing one.
searchedFor: looked for scripts/*.spec.ts / test dir for scripts

samples.summary: YorkieService's JWT_SECRET-unset branch (no injector + warning) is untested
samples.evidence: `yorkie.service.spec.ts`'s `createMockConfigService` always returns a `JWT_SECRET`, and the two new tests only assert the scoped token for a configured secret. The documented fallback — warn and hand the SDK `authTokenInjector: undefined` rather than throwing — has no test, so a change that made this throw (breaking seed commands/integration tools that construct the service with a bare config) would pass the suite.

samples.summary: Divider resize math change (`track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`, 25px width, touch-action) has no test
samples.evidence: The diff changes the split-pane drag math from `ratio = (clientX - left) / rect.width` to `/ track`, triples the divider width, and adds `touch-action: none`. `packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts` gains two read-only tests but nothing that dispatches pointer events on the divider or asserts pane flex-basis after a drag; grep of the test file shows no `note-divider`/pointer usage. A wrong `track` (e.g. divider not laid out yet in jsdom → offsetWidth 0) would silently restore the old off-by-divider-width behavior with no failing test.

samples.summary: 'a read-only mount still reads presence' asserts only that an array is returned
samples.evidence: `expect(Array.isArray(store.getPresences())).toBe(true)` holds whether or not presence reads are actually preserved — on an unattached local document there are no presences to see, so the test would pass with `getPresences()` hard-coded to `[]` or gated by `readOnly` returning `[]`. The stated behavior ("a viewer sees the peers they cannot announce themselves to") needs a peer presence in the document and a non-empty read to be pinned.

samples.summary: A couple of assertions in the read-only wrapper test are trivially true
samples.evidence: In 'forwards reads and subscriptions', `expect(view.canUndo()).toBe(false)` is true for a fresh `MemNoteStore` regardless of whether the wrapper forwards `canUndo` at all (a neutered `canUndo` would also be falsy-ish — though `undefined()` would throw, so this is weak rather than fully vacuous). Likewise `expect(view.getPeerSelections()).toEqual([])` matches `MemNoteStore`'s hard-coded `[]`. The forwarding claim would be pinned better against a store with real history/peers.

samples.summary: Shared-notes-layout test asserts non-persistence only for viewMode, and mocks the uploader it checks
samples.evidence: The file header claims '...with nothing written back to the visitor's stored preferences', but only `wafflebase:notes:viewMode` is asserted unchanged; `keymap` and `showAuthors` (both wired to bare `setState` with no persistence) are never toggled or checked, so a future `writeKeymap` slipping in would not fail. Separately, 'hands the share-token uploader to the view' mocks `shareTokenImageUploader` to return `uploaded:${token}`, so it verifies prop plumbing only — acceptable for a wiring test, but it cannot catch a wrong uploader being selected for a viewer beyond the `undefined` assertion.
searchedFor: grep notes-settings read/write helpers usage in shared-notes-layout.tsx

verdict.reason: Verified the behavior exists and is untested. yorkie-doc-store.ts:604-608 adds the `readOnly` constructor flag; the two presence gates are real at :1263 (publishResolvedLocalCursor) and :3199 (updateCursorPos). A repo-wide search for a two-argument construction (`YorkieDocStore\([^)]*,`) returns exactly one hit, the production caller docs-view.tsx:364 — no test anywhere constructs the store read-only. Every test construction is single-arg (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:36/242/649/730/749/805/840/903, editor-undo-selection.test.ts:102/167/262, helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:111/137), so all of them run with readOnly=false and would pass unchanged if the gates were deleted. The presence key both gates write, `activeCursorPos`, appears in no test file in the repository. The existing presence tests (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:359-596, 853-868) assert the write happens, and the only read-only-adjacent docs tests (docs-find-bar-read-only, docs-context-menu, docs-table-context-menu) cover UI gating, not the Yorkie presence write; the sibling coverage in tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts:68 is for the sheets YorkieStore. No e2e suite covers docs. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric as a major missing-test gap: a regression reintroducing the viewer presence write ships silently and wedges the share-link viewer's sync, a user-visible path.

Neither is the call-site change in `sheet-view.tsx` (`runRemoteSync(!readOnly)`, `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : …)`) covered by any frontend test — grep for `readOnly` in packages/frontend/tests returns no sheet-view file.

verdict.reason: The guard exists as claimed at packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:973-976 (read-only => worksheet.render() and return, skipping the persisting recalc pass). No test anywhere in the repo exercises it: a repo-wide grep for `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` yields test hits only on the model `Sheet` (packages/sheets/test/sheet/cross-sheet-calculation.test.ts:138,176,212,228,258; cross-sheet-cycle.test.ts:61-188) and the Yorkie integration file (packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-cross-sheet.integration.ts:41,85, writable env, skipped without YORKIE_RPC_ADDR). Repo-wide greps for `new Spreadsheet` and `Spreadsheet.prototype` return no test at all, so nothing can reach the view-class `_readOnly` branch. Existing read-only suites cover other layers only: packages/sheets/test/view/worksheet-readonly-editing.test.ts (Worksheet.finishEditing) and packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts (presence, ensureAxisOrder, comment writes). The call-site composition in sheet-view.tsx:1308,1322 is inline in the effect, not in a helper, and remote-change-utils.test.ts covers only needsRecalc(ops) with no readOnly dimension. Impact is major: YorkieStore gates only presence (:651), axis growth (:689) and comments (:1311), not cell writes, so this guard is the real defense against a share-link viewer's mount writing the CRDT and wedging their sync; a regression would ship silently.

finding.summary: `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` read-only early-return is untested, and so is `sheet-view`'s `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` gate
finding.evidence: The diff adds `if (this._readOnly) { this.worksheet.render(); return; }` to `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` and calls it the engine-level backstop ('so neither this call site nor a future one can leak it'). `grep recalculateCrossSheetFormulas packages/sheets` shows tests only for `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (test/sheet/cross-sheet-*.test.ts), none constructing a read-only `Spreadsheet`; the only read-only view test, test/view/worksheet-readonly-editing.test.ts, covers `finishEditing` only. Frontend-side, `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` and `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : …)` in sheet-view.tsx have no test either (no sheet-view test file). A regression re-enables a viewer's recalc write, which the webhook refuses and which wedges that viewer's sync — the exact failure this change exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists: spreadsheet.ts:971-979 adds the read-only early return in recalculateCrossSheetFormulas, and sheet-view.tsx:1308/1322 gate runRemoteSync/scheduleRemoteSync on readOnly. I searched well beyond the reviewer's paths and found no covering test. No test in packages/sheets constructs a Spreadsheet at all (grep 'Spreadsheet' in packages/sheets/test matches only isSpreadsheetHtml in model/grids.test.ts), so the engine gate is unexercised; cross-sheet-calculation/cycle tests drive model-level Sheet with no read-only mode. On the frontend, packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet is NOT empty (the reviewer's glob claim was wrong), but neither candidate covers the gate: yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts exercises presence seeding, updateSelection, ensureAxisOrder and comment mutators only, and yorkie-store.ts gates only those three paths (:109, :651, :689, assertWritable :1310) — cell/batch writes are not store-gated, so it gives no indirect coverage of the recalc write. remote-change-utils.test.ts tests needsRecalc(ops) classification with ops passed directly and never touches readOnly. There is no sheet-view test file anywhere (glob **/*sheet-view* matches only the source) and no e2e/playwright/integration test dirs. So a regression re-enabling a viewer's recalc write — a webhook-refused write that wedges that viewer's sync — would ship undetected: major under the missing-tests branch of the test-adequacy rubric.
